questions.stem: What is time to first token in a generative model response?

options.A: The average speed of producing each following word after the first
options.B: The delay before the first word of the answer appears
options.C: The total time until the complete answer has been delivered
options.D: The time spent waiting in a background job queue before work starts

questions.rationale: Time to first token is the delay before the first word appears. Time per output token is later speed, and total response time covers the full answer.

questions.stem: What is prompt injection in a generative AI system?

options.A: Placing instructions in content the model reads to change behaviour
options.B: Encrypting every retrieved passage before it enters the model prompt
options.C: Raising model temperature so every answer becomes more creative
options.D: Deleting unused tools from the allow-list after each finished request

questions.rationale: Prompt injection places instructions inside content the model reads so the system behaviour changes. Encryption, temperature, and tool cleanup are separate controls.

questions.stem: What must observability logs avoid recording?

options.A: The model name used for a successful request and its version
options.B: Whether a cache entry answered the request without a new call
options.C: Passwords, keys, or personal data from the request
options.D: How long each retrieval stage took to finish for that request

questions.rationale: Logs should record operational detail such as model, timing, and cache use. They must not store passwords, keys, or personal data.

questions.stem: How does an exact-match cache differ from a prompt cache?

options.A: Exact-match cache only shortens streaming display for waiting users
options.B: Prompt cache only stores complete answers for identical user questions
options.C: Exact-match cache deletes embeddings after every failed model call
options.D: Exact-match reuses one answer; prompt cache reuses a prompt start

questions.rationale: An exact-match cache returns a stored answer for the same question. A prompt cache reuses a repeated prompt beginning to cut input cost and delay.

questions.stem: How does indirect prompt injection differ from direct injection?

options.A: Indirect injection only works when streaming output is turned off
options.B: Indirect injection hides instructions in material the system later reads
options.C: Direct injection can only change temperature and maximum output tokens
options.D: Direct injection never appears inside a recorded authenticated user session

questions.rationale: Direct injection is written by the user. Indirect injection hides instructions in documents, pages, or other content the system will read later.

questions.stem: Which cost reduction method should be tried first?

options.A: Caching, because it can reduce both cost and delay
options.B: Always switching every request to the largest available model
options.C: Removing timeouts so slow calls keep waiting for longer periods
options.D: Logging full personal data for every failed request in plain text

questions.rationale: Day 4 orders cost methods with caching first, because it is the only method that reduces both cost and delay.

questions.stem: What is the main purpose of a rate limit?

options.A: To replace evaluation metrics with a single monthly spend total
options.B: To force every request onto the largest available model option
options.C: To stop one user from exhausting capacity needed by others
options.D: To store passwords and access keys inside application log files

questions.rationale: A rate limit caps how much service one user can consume in a period so capacity stays available for everyone.

questions.stem: Which outcome returns text that looks certain but has no error signal?

options.A: A temporary timeout that can succeed on a later retry attempt
options.B: A permanent rejection caused by an invalid or unauthorised request
options.C: A capacity refusal after a quota or limit has been exceeded
options.D: A confident wrong reply that only monitoring later detects

questions.rationale: Silent failure produces a confident wrong answer with no error. Temporary, permanent, and capacity failures still surface as system conditions.

questions.stem: Why must control stay outside the model for irreversible tool actions?

options.A: Because larger models never request tools during normal inference
options.B: Because fixed policy and permissions decide what may run
options.C: Because prompt caching removes the need for any tool allow-list
options.D: Because streaming alone prevents every prompt injection attempt

questions.rationale: Injection can change what the model requests. Damage is limited only when application policy, sandboxing, and least privilege sit outside the model.

questions.stem: A dependency fails often during peak load. Which recovery pair fits best?

options.A: Use a circuit breaker, then a reduced honest fallback
options.B: Remove all timeouts so every slow call can finish eventually
options.C: Retry forever with no delay until the background queue empties
options.D: Disable metrics so operators stop seeing the repeated failures

questions.rationale: When failures are frequent, a circuit breaker stops hammering the dependency and a fallback still gives a reduced but honest response.
